name: lighthouse
description: Lighthouse Labs perpetual decentralized storage (lighthouse.storage) — API-key uploads to IPFS/Filecoin with perpetual pinning, gateway retrieval, and a bridge that registers every CID in the store module so it gets the store's visibility, grants, pools and marketplace without the store holding the bytes. API + console, mod-protocol wallet auth, bring-your-own-key.
frontend: app/server.py (stdlib — the console at /lighthouse on :50681; proxies /lighthouse/_api to the API)

store.auth: the caller's own protocol token is forwarded — this module holds no store credential, so the store's whitelist, terms and quota apply to the address that actually signed
store.note: the store keeps the gateway url, so store /get redirects a reader straight at Lighthouse; no bytes are copied into the store

/status.docs: Module status: key configured, gateway, index size, auth mode, and the store link (whitelist / terms / quota when a token is sent)

/me.docs: Caller address, owner flag, which Lighthouse key this request would use, and the store's view of the caller

/key.docs: GET key status (+ remote validation); POST (owner) persist the deployment key off-chain in ~/.mod/lighthouse/credentials.json

/put.docs: Upload a file to Lighthouse (perpetual IPFS/Filecoin pin); form: key, register=true, public, pool. Registers the CID in the store unless register=false

/put/text.docs: Same as /put for a string body: {text, key, register, public, pool}

/get.docs: Stream a CID through the Lighthouse gateway (?download=1 to attach). Public by construction — access control is the store's job

/preview.docs: Peek at a CID: decoded text when it is text, size, truncated flag

/list.docs: This module's index: the caller's uploads (?scope=all for every row, owner only)

/pin.docs: Record a CID in the index (Lighthouse uploads are already pinned perpetually)

/rm.docs: Drop a row from the index. Does NOT unpin — the pin is perpetual and the CID stays retrievable

/usage.docs: Remote data usage for the key this request is using

/uploads.docs: What Lighthouse itself lists under this key (?page=)

/store.docs: The store link from the caller's side: reachable, address, whitelisted, terms accepted, quota, and what still blocks a push

/store/terms.docs: The store's current terms text + version

/store/terms/accept.docs: Sign-accept the store terms — the caller's own token is forwarded as the proof, this module never signs for anybody

/store/register.docs: Reference an existing Lighthouse CID in the store: {cid, key, size, public, pool}. No bytes move

/store/objects.docs: The caller's store objects, Lighthouse-backed only unless ?all_backends=1

/store/mirror.docs: Make a store object perpetual: fetch it with the caller's token, upload to Lighthouse, register the CID back. Reports whether the CID came back identical

/mcp.docs: MCP. GET is the whole schema as a document (protocol, transports, auth, every tool inputSchema, client config); POST is the Streamable HTTP JSON-RPC 2.0 transport. A tools/call for a tool that acts for a signer needs the caller Bearer token, which is forwarded to the store exactly as the REST routes do

/mcp/tools.docs: Just the tools: name, description, inputSchema, annotations, which auth and which transports each one accepts

/mcp/config.docs: Client config for this deployment — http block, stdio block, and the `claude mcp add` line, with the url as the caller reached it

byok.note: a per-request Lighthouse key, never written to disk and discarded when the request ends — how a visitor uses the console without trusting the box's key

transports.http: POST /mcp on the API — schema at GET /mcp
transports.stdio: python3 mcp.py — runs with this box’s own keys

mcp.auth: the caller’s mod-protocol token as Authorization: Bearer, same as the REST routes; lighthouse_status, lighthouse_preview and lighthouse_store need none
mcp.byok: the `key` argument (or `api_key` on the upload tools) spends the caller’s Lighthouse account and is never written to disk
mcp.note: one implementation behind three faces — the MCP tools, the REST routes and the CLI all call mod.py and store_link.py, so the schema the console renders is the server’s own

env.LIGHTHOUSE_API_KEY: API key from files.lighthouse.storage (or persist via m lighthouse/set_key)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_DIR: State dir: credentials, owner claim, sqlite index (default ~/.mod/lighthouse)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_ACTIVATOR_URL: Fleet activator used to wake a slept store (default http://127.0.0.1:9000; empty string = never wake, just report it down)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_STORE_MODULE: Activator's name for the store module (default 'store')
env.LIGHTHOUSE_WAKE_TIMEOUT: Seconds to wait for a woken store's api port (default 45)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_OPEN: 1 = treat every caller as signed in (local development only)
env.LIGHTHOUSE_OWNER: Fallback owner address when ~/.mod/lighthouse/owner.json is absent
